title: Pre-flight prints the same guider problem twice and both times tells you to connect PHD2, in a build that ships its own native guider
summary: Two halves, one already closed and one still live. The DUPLICATION was fixed by an earlier wave: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/equipment_rules.dart:105-148 now emits per-node 'Guider Not Connected' warnings and keeps the generic 'No Guider Connected' summary as a fallback ONLY when no enabled node can be attributed, with a regression test already in place. The BACKEND-AWARENESS half was still real and is now fixed. The old text said '<node> requires a guider (PHD2)' and, unconditionally, 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' I confirmed against the Guiding panel that this is bad advice, not just imprecise: desktop_sections.dart:230 only renders a Connect button when `isPhd2Guider` is true, and for any other backend it renders an 'Equipment' button (desktop_sections.dart:252) that navigates away. This build discovers and connects a 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:779), so an operator running the native guider was sent to a panel with no Connect button on it. The rule now drops PHD2 from the description and routes the hint through a new `_guiderResolutionHint(GuiderState)`: PHD2 selected -> 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.'; another backend selected -> 'Connect <device name> in the Equipment panel.'; nothing selected -> 'Connect a guider in the Equipment panel - the built-in multi-star guider, or PHD2.' The hint is computed once and shared by both the per-node warnings and the fallback summary, so the two cannot drift.

title: Node palette search ranks Smart Exposure above the node literally named 'Dither' when you search 'Dither'
summary: The location named in the finding is already correct - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_palette.dart:54 and .../sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:35 both route through the shared `rankNodePaletteMatches` (node_palette_search.dart), which scores exact name 100 / prefix 80 / name-substring 60 / description 20 and hoists the best-scoring category, with tests in sequencer_jank_p3_test.dart. But a THIRD node-palette search box was still running the old, unranked filter: the Insert Above / Insert Below picker reached from the tree's right-click menu (`_InsertNodePicker` in sequence_tree_context_menu.dart) filtered on `name.contains(q) || description.contains(q)` and rendered survivors in catalogue order, so typing 'Dither' there still put Smart Exposure first - the exact failure the finding describes, on the surface a user reaches when they right-click to insert a node at a specific slot. Moved it onto the shared ranker.

title: Continue Session reports '0 minutes integration' for a session that has 12s of integration on the card behind it
summary: Real, and the finding's `screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart` unit is the wrong file - the Progress row is built by packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:324-340 (the 'Continue Session' dialog) and formatted by `_formatIntegration(double hours)` at :134, which returned `'${hours.toStringAsFixed(1)} hours'` above 1h and `'${(hours*60).round()} minutes'` below it. 12s = 0.0033h rounds to 0, so a run with four real light frames on disk announced '0 minutes integration'. Fixed at the cause by giving the app ONE integration formatter: new `formatIntegrationSeconds` / `formatIntegrationHours` in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/utils/duration_format.dart (h/m/s, rounding to whole seconds first so 59.6s reads '1m 0s' not '60s', and clamping negative/non-finite to '0s'). `ParsedRunStats.formatDuration` - the formatter the dashboard's last-night recap card, the history tab and the post-session dialog already render - now delegates to it, and the Continue Session dialog calls it too, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about the same run. 12s now reads '12s' in both places.

title: A node can only be reordered by drag; the node context menu offers just Duplicate and Delete
summary: The finding's inventory of the menu is stale - the right-click menu already carried eight entries (Skip to here, Insert Above, Insert Below, Duplicate, Group into Sequential, Group into Parallel, Disable/Enable, Delete), and Move Up / Move Down already existed in the row's kebab 'More Actions' menu (node_item.dart:937-962), so drag was NOT the only route. What was real: the right-click menu itself had no reorder, which is the menu an operator opens when they want to move a node; and the in-code justification for that split cited a 'Shift+Up / Shift+Down keyboard shortcut wired in sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart' that does not reorder anything - kSequenceTreeShortcuts:68-71 binds Shift+Arrow to EXTEND THE SELECTION. Added Move Up / Move Down to SequenceTreeContextMenu, going through the same `moveNode(id, parentId, index)` call the kebab and drag-drop use (one undo entry shape, one reindex path), disabled with an explanatory tooltip on the root and at either end of a sibling list. Corrected the false comment in node_item.dart rather than leaving a note that misdescribes the keymap.
